sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Best guide and build for Baizhi from WW (Wuthering Waves). Baizhi is a 4 ★ rarity character from the Glacio element who uses the Rectifier type weapon.
 Baizhi is a researcher in Remnant Ecoacoustics. Baizhi's once unfulfilled wish has now manifested as her loyal companion. The Remnant Creature You'tan is her source of healing powers, and a lifelong research focus.

sections.heading: Pros
Cons
Review
sections.text:
Baizhi is a 4 star free Glacio Rectifier Support that brings a wide array of buffs and healing utilities for her teammates, filling a niche that is necessary to have in any meta team composition. This alone is enough to make her a viable character; however, it is worth nothing she has a lot of specifics to her kit. For one, her buffs only apply to one team member at a time, making her incompatible with coordinated attackers. But it gets more complicated than that.
 Her Forte gauge can accumulate up to 4 stacks, each generated by performing one of her Basic Attacks. It can be depleted one of two ways: with her Skill, or her Heavy Attack. Depleting this Forte bar is not only necessary to her rotation as it generates a big chunk of Concerto energy, enabling her to trigger her Outro skill buffs as soon as possible, but it also regenerates health every 2 seconds for any character that is on the field. Meaning the healing applies even if you switch to a different character than Baizhi.
 Her Resonance Skill calls her companion You’tan back to her, which pulses Glacio DMG around herself after a short delay while simultaneously healing her whole team. Depending on the amount of Forte stacks you have, this can generate a lot of Concerto energy.
 Her Ultimate generates a good chunk of Concerto energy as well while healing her whole team. But that’s not all: periodically, a total of 4 (6 at sequence 4) Remnant Entities are launched at an enemy every 2.5 seconds, providing damage and healing, counting as a Coordinated Attack.
 Finally, her Inherent Skill 1 is very useful as it provides a 15% attack buff to any character who picks up the Euphonia her Resonance Skill generates for 20 seconds. This Euphonia appears as a feather on the ground, which can be picked up by a single character who sports the buff, which persists upon switching out. However, as only one character can receive that buff at a time, making sure to pick up that buff with your Main DPS given every character teleports in front of their enemy when casting their Intro Skill can prove to be quite tricky. It is therefore recommended to swap out to your Main DPS after casting your Baizhi’s Resonance Skill and to go pick it up to make sure they are the one sporting the buff. Hence, hybrids with long rotations aren’t recommended with the character, as the shorter your hybrid’s rotation is, the more your Main DPS can utilize that buff.
 In the meta, this places Baizhi in an awkward position: while she provides Coordinated attacks, she isn’t compatible with other Coordinated attackers, meaning she isn’t good in Jinhsi teams that typically run two. Her rotation is not as fast as Verina’s and her buffs aren’t as potent as Shorekeeper’s, who she shares similar field time with; hence, there is no reason to privilege Baizhi over the two 5 star generalist support options; lastly, her Euphonia buff can simply make her uncomfortable to play and can see players forfeiting the buff altogether or forfeiting the character altogether.
 To summarize, Baizhi is a character who has the potential to provide many buffs to one character she switches into at a time, but due to her mid-length rotation time and good, but not crazy buffing potential, she falls short to the 5 star generalists, who do everything she does, only better. Her awkward rotations if you wish to capitalize on her buffs don’t do her justice, but she remains a good free generalist option close to any team can run and be completely fine with.

sections.heading: Best Weapons
sections.text:
The percentages show the performance of the weapon based on calculations , but in some cases, some weapons might provide additional QOL that can't be quantified and it would push that weapon ahead of others in the priority (and in those cases, we would put that weapon higher).

 1

 Stellar Symphony (R 1 )

 Shorekeeper’s signature weapon is not only amazing for her but also for any Rectifier support. Granting insane amounts of Energy Regen as its secondary stat, increasing the equipped character’s HP all the while providing additional Concerto Energy when casting your Ultimate is seriously valuable for any support that can equip the weapon. It additionally provides a team-wide ATK buff if the equipped character’s Resonance Skill is used and it provides healing, which makes it stand out as an amazing support weapon.
 2

 Variation (R 5 )

 A utility-focused weapon prioritizing lightning-fast Concerto rotations over raw output with the ability to transform entire units' action priorities under the right circumstances. Not always a good choice but when implemented correctly makes all the difference. Also offers an immense amount of Energy Regen further accelerating rotations and supportive capabilities.
 3

 Call of the Abyss (R 5 )

 Best weapon choice if you don't have Concerto weapons available, acquired for free via Rinascita Exploration Quests, which gives a great amount of Energy Regen and an extra Healing Bonus boost upon casting Ultimate for higher sustain.
 4

 Rectifier of Voyager (R 5 )

 An easily accessible supportive option with a reasonable amount of Energy Regen. It also grants the unique ability to gain a sizable chunk of raw Resonance Energy once every 20 seconds. For most character's rotations in teams, this bonus will be ready every time it's their turn to switch-in, making this weapon a great choice for any character who doesn't need damage but needs their Ultimate fast and has trouble accessing it otherwise. The flat energy gain is more powerful the less energy the character and team they are a part of can generate. This weapon is preferred over certain 4-star Rectifier options that give Energy Regen such as Rectifier#25 as the flat Energy boost from this weapon's passive is more effective at granting Resonance Energy.
 5

 Rectifier#25 (R 5 )

 Decent F2P craftable option that provides a lot of Energy Regen, some additional HP restore and some ATK% depending on your current HP situation. Little value beyond the Energy Regen and small ATK% boost.

sections.heading: Best Echo Sets
sections.text:
1

Rejuvenating Glow

 Offers a 10% unconditional Healing% boost and an most importantly a 15% ATK% boost for the entire team, lasting 30 seconds whenever you heal yourself or any of your allies. This bonus can be triggered by character abilities and weapon effects, is easy to keep active 100% of the time and is a big help for all party members.
 Below you can find Main Echo options:

 Fallacy of No Return

 - Grants 10% increased Energy Regeneration for the wearer and a team wide 10% ATK boost on use for 20 seconds. A strong option for those looking to generate as much energy as possible or who favor a more permanent party buffing effect compared to Bell-Borne Geochelone.

 Bell-Borne Geochelone

 - While nowadays a worse option for the Rejuvenating Glow set for damage than the Fallacy of No Return due to a shorter buff uptime, only granting 10% DMG Bonus for 15 seconds, the Bell-Borne Geochelone remains a good choice if you don't have a good Fallacy to use for the set. It also has increased survivability by blocking 50% of the damage from a max of 3 hits if you desire to have that in your team.

sections.heading: Special Echo Sets
sections.text:
Moonlit Clouds

 Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.
 Below you can find Main Echo options:

 Impermanence Heron

 - Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

sections.heading: Rotation
sections.text:
Concerto weapon cuts down on the final amount of basics you have to do, hence it’s best to equip on Baizhi for overall Team DPS (you want to spend the least amount of time on her). If you don’t have your intro skill, add an extra basic attack.
 This rotation isn’t always going to repeat itself as you will have stacks built up from previous rotations. Use skill whenever you’ve built 4 stacks, and heavy attack if you don’t have skill. It should make this rotation faster than what’s on paper here.

 Pros & Cons
 Pros
 Incredible supportive Outro, granting all-type DMG Amplification which is not lost when switching;

 Good healing enabling for good survivability, especially with Sequences involved (which can also buff Glacio DMG at S6);

 Very universal buffs, enabling her to slot into most teams;

 Is effectively a free character;

 Can grant the team a cheat death ability after unlocking S5 in the form of a full heal to the character that would have suffered fatal damage.

 Cons
 Is in direct competition with the very similar but superior Shorekeeper and Verina, the former of which provides more significant buffs and the latter of which has a much shorter rotation time;

 A lot of her buffs aren’t compatible with Coordinated attackers;

 Picking up her Euphonia buff can make rotations awkward and be annoying;

 Rotations can get longer due to being close to static when attacking, sometimes forcing dodges;

 Close to all of her attacks have a slight delay due to her pet needing to perform attacks for her.

 Review
 Baizhi is a 4 star free Glacio Rectifier Support that brings a wide array of buffs and healing utilities for her teammates, filling a niche that is necessary to have in any meta team composition. This alone is enough to make her a viable character; however, it is worth nothing she has a lot of specifics to her kit. For one, her buffs only apply to one team member at a time, making her incompatible with coordinated attackers. But it gets more complicated than that.
 Her Forte gauge can accumulate up to 4 stacks, each generated by performing one of her Basic Attacks. It can be depleted one of two ways: with her Skill, or her Heavy Attack. Depleting this Forte bar is not only necessary to her rotation as it generates a big chunk of Concerto energy, enabling her to trigger her Outro skill buffs as soon as possible, but it also regenerates health every 2 seconds for any character that is on the field. Meaning the healing applies even if you switch to a different character than Baizhi.
 Her Resonance Skill calls her companion You’tan back to her, which pulses Glacio DMG around herself after a short delay while simultaneously healing her whole team. Depending on the amount of Forte stacks you have, this can generate a lot of Concerto energy.
 Her Ultimate generates a good chunk of Concerto energy as well while healing her whole team. But that’s not all: periodically, a total of 4 (6 at sequence 4) Remnant Entities are launched at an enemy every 2.5 seconds, providing damage and healing, counting as a Coordinated Attack.
 Finally, her Inherent Skill 1 is very useful as it provides a 15% attack buff to any character who picks up the Euphonia her Resonance Skill generates for 20 seconds. This Euphonia appears as a feather on the ground, which can be picked up by a single character who sports the buff, which persists upon switching out. However, as only one character can receive that buff at a time, making sure to pick up that buff with your Main DPS given every character teleports in front of their enemy when casting their Intro Skill can prove to be quite tricky. It is therefore recommended to swap out to your Main DPS after casting your Baizhi’s Resonance Skill and to go pick it up to make sure they are the one sporting the buff. Hence, hybrids with long rotations aren’t recommended with the character, as the shorter your hybrid’s rotation is, the more your Main DPS can utilize that buff.
 In the meta, this places Baizhi in an awkward position: while she provides Coordinated attacks, she isn’t compatible with other Coordinated attackers, meaning she isn’t good in Jinhsi teams that typically run two. Her rotation is not as fast as Verina’s and her buffs aren’t as potent as Shorekeeper’s, who she shares similar field time with; hence, there is no reason to privilege Baizhi over the two 5 star generalist support options; lastly, her Euphonia buff can simply make her uncomfortable to play and can see players forfeiting the buff altogether or forfeiting the character altogether.
 To summarize, Baizhi is a character who has the potential to provide many buffs to one character she switches into at a time, but due to her mid-length rotation time and good, but not crazy buffing potential, she falls short to the 5 star generalists, who do everything she does, only better. Her awkward rotations if you wish to capitalize on her buffs don’t do her justice, but she remains a good free generalist option close to any team can run and be completely fine with.

 Shorekeeper’s signature weapon is not only amazing for her but also for any Rectifier support.  A utility-focused weapon prioritizing lightning-fast Concerto rotations over raw output with the ability to transform entire units' action priorities under the right circumstances.  3

 4

 Rectifier of Voyager (R 5 )

 An easily accessible supportive option with a reasonable amount of Energy Regen. It also grants the unique ability to gain a sizable chunk of raw Resonance Energy once every 20 seconds. For most character's rotations in teams, this bonus will be ready every time it's their turn to switch-in, making this weapon a great choice for any character who doesn't need damage but needs their Ultimate fast and has trouble accessing it otherwise. The flat energy gain is more powerful the less energy the character and team they are a part of can generate. This weapon is preferred over certain 4-star Rectifier options that give Energy Regen such as Rectifier#25 as the flat Energy boost from this weapon's passive is more effective at granting Resonance Energy.
